builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Vendster: An Evaluation Arena to Investigate How Forecasting Tool Quality Affects LLM Agent Behaviors in Buyer-Vendor Negotiation
summary: It replaces accuracy-first selection of forecast tools with a negotiation arena that measures downstream decision value under controlled bias and interval width. It costs added evaluation complexity, repeated LLM rollouts, and domain customization rather than new model training or cluster-scale infrastructure. It can fail when the arena’s buyer-vendor setting, agent reactivity, or sampled demand patterns do not transfer to the reader’s production workflow.
rationale: The paper is useful for evaluation design, but its evidence is tied to a specific LLM negotiation arena rather than a broadly validated production replacement for standard forecasting metrics.
technique: Decision-value evaluation arena for forecasting tools

It costs added evaluation complexity, repeated LLM rollouts, and domain customization rather than new model training or cluster-scale infrastructure. It can fail when the arena’s buyer-vendor setting, agent reactivity, or sampled demand patterns do not transfer to the reader’s production workflow.
Model-generated forecasts raise sales target attainment by up to +17 percentage points (p<0.001); relWQL and MASE do not significantly predict negotiation outcomes.
